structured.approach: Attempt 2 fixes the two G2 refusals. Attempt 1 cited a directory and a data file that I had not opened with Read. This time I read every repository file the output cites: pipeline.py, ingest.py, transform.py, dq.py, schedule.json, __init__.py, data/sample_feed.csv, README.md and CLAUDE.md. Each claim now cites the exact file it relies on. I dropped the claim based only on a search, because search results are not a citable file. I also dropped the description of the sample feed as 'synthetic', because no file I read says that. The step itself works as before: feat.design and feat.tasks set the storage scope and the file budgets of the Data Engineering tasks, and the tool view plus the source files confirm there is no database. The output is an empty change register, the logical paid_date change is sent to DE-05, and DQ-1 is carried as a non-blocking question. The file on disk had a '[Tool result]' line added after my attempt-1 text. It was not part of the template, and the tool view it repeats is cited in section 3, so the full rewrite leaves it out. No connector was used, and no production data was read.

claims.text: The feature design lists storage, database and schema migration as out of scope; the data change is one new record key paid_date, one new reject reason 'paid_date' and in-memory structures.
DD-1 rules out any new repository, service, runtime, library or storage, and NF-10 makes every new function pure and in-memory with no I/O and no network.
Adding storage or a network call from the libraries would reopen DES-01, and the design triggers none of these.

TSK-01 may change src/ap_pipeline/transform.py, src/ap_pipeline/__init__.py (version step only) and tests/test_pipeline.py; TSK-02 adds src/ap_pipeline/delays.py and tests/test_delays.py; neither lists a DDL file, migration or table.
TSK-01 must not change ingest.py, dq.py, pipeline.py or schedule.json.
ap_pipeline has no database; no migrations exist or are required.
pipeline.run chains parse_feed, to_model and quality_report and returns (records, report) in memory; nothing is written to a store.
parse_feed reads CSV text with csv.DictReader over io.StringIO.
to_model imports only datetime, decimal and typing and maps rows to dicts with id, vendor, due_date, amount and paid.
quality_report computes rows, loaded, rejected and reject_reasons as a dict.
schedule.json holds only frequency daily, time 02:00 and timezone Asia/Kolkata, with no connection settings.
data/sample_feed.csv is a flat CSV file with header invoice_id,vendor,due_date,amount,paid and no paid_date column.
The repository is Python 3.9 standard library.
The README describes the flow as vendor invoice feed to Invoice Data Model to data-quality report.
The invoice record (DC-1) is a plain Python dict with paid_date added as a key; this logical change belongs to DE-05, not to a physical database change.
No input names the production component that wires the stages and carries CT-1 (DQ-1).
Decisions D-2026-031, D-2026-044, D-2026-050 and lessons L-007, L-011 do not require storage.

open_questions: DBQ-1 (non-blocking, carried from feat.design DQ-1): a database change would be needed only if the production host that wires the stages later stored records, overdue rows or risk levels. None is needed in this feature. Owner: Architect.

The design puts storage, databases and schema migrations out of scope, and the Data Engineering tasks TSK-01 and TSK-02 change only Python modules and tests. ap_pipeline has no database: each source file I read works in memory, and the sample feed is a flat CSV. Both G2 refusals are fixed by citing only files I read in this step. task.db_changes was rewritten in full with an empty change register, and there are no blocking questions.
